questions.stem: Starch and cellulose are both polymers of glucose, yet humans can digest starch but not cellulose. What explains this difference?

options.text: Cellulose contains different elements than starch
The glucose monomers are linked differently — humans have enzymes to break the linkages in starch but not the linkages in cellulose
Cellulose is not actually a polymer
Starch is smaller than cellulose and fits into our stomachs

questions.explanation: Both starch and cellulose are made from glucose monomers, but the glycosidic bonds linking them have different orientations (alpha in starch, beta in cellulose). Human digestive enzymes (amylase) can break the alpha linkages in starch but cannot break the beta linkages in cellulose. This is why cellulose passes through our digestive system as dietary fibre.

questions.stem: Proteins are natural condensation polymers made from amino acid monomers. Each amino acid has an -NH₂ group and a -COOH group. What type of bond forms between amino acids?

options.text: Ester bonds, releasing water
Peptide bonds (amide linkages), releasing water
Ionic bonds, releasing hydrogen
Glycosidic bonds, releasing carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: When the -NH₂ group of one amino acid reacts with the -COOH group of another, a peptide bond (-CONH-) forms and water is released. This is the same amide linkage found in nylon, which is why nylon is sometimes described as an artificial protein. Long chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds form polypeptides (proteins).

questions.stem: DNA is a natural polymer. Its monomers are nucleotides. Unlike synthetic polymers that repeat the same monomer, DNA uses four different nucleotides. Why is this variation important?

options.text: Different nucleotides give DNA different colours
The specific sequence of four nucleotides encodes genetic information, like letters forming words
DNA would not be a polymer if it used only one nucleotide
Using four nucleotides makes DNA stronger

questions.explanation: DNA uses four nucleotides (containing bases A, T, C, G) in specific sequences that encode genetic information. Just as 26 letters form millions of different words, 4 nucleotide bases in different sequences can encode all the information needed to build and run an organism. This is fundamentally different from synthetic polymers where identical monomers repeat.

questions.stem: Biodegradable plastics like polylactic acid (PLA) are made from natural monomers (lactic acid from corn starch). Why are these considered more environmentally friendly than traditional plastics?

options.text: They are stronger and last longer
They can be broken down by microorganisms, use renewable resources, and do not persist in the environment
They produce no carbon dioxide when manufactured
They are cheaper to produce than traditional plastics

questions.explanation: PLA is a condensation polymer with ester linkages that microorganisms can break down through hydrolysis. It is made from renewable plant sources (not crude oil), and it decomposes in composting conditions rather than persisting for centuries in landfill. However, it requires specific composting conditions and is not as durable as conventional plastics.

questions.stem: Silk and wool are natural protein fibres, while cotton is a natural cellulose fibre. A student accidentally spills concentrated acid on both fabrics. Which fabric would be damaged more and why?

options.text: Cotton, because cellulose is weaker than protein
Silk and wool, because acid can hydrolyse the peptide bonds in proteins
Neither would be damaged by acid
Both would be damaged equally

questions.explanation: Concentrated acid catalyses the hydrolysis of peptide bonds in protein fibres like silk and wool, breaking the polymer chains and destroying the fabric. Cotton (cellulose) is more resistant to acid hydrolysis because the glycosidic bonds in cellulose are harder to break under acidic conditions. This is why protein-based fabrics require more careful handling.
